q: 1. The discharge in the minor distributaries will be generally less than .............
explain: In the canal hierarchy, minor distributaries are small channels carrying low discharge (typically less than 0.25 m3/s) directly to the field outlets.

q: 2. If Q is the discharge, the wetted perimeter of a regime channel according to Lacey's theory is given by .............
explain: Lacey's perimeter equation is P = 4.75 * sqrt(Q). This is a fundamental regime equation used to design stable alluvial channels.

q: 3. If d is the mean diameter of the silt particles the Lacey's silt factor f is proportional to .............
explain: Lacey's silt factor 'f' is calculated using the formula f = 1.76 * sqrt(dm), where dm is the mean particle size in mm.

q: 4. Falls in the canals are provided when .............
options: natural ground slope is same as the design slope
natural ground slope is more than the design slope
natural ground slope is less than the design slope
the canal runs in deep cutting
explain: When the ground drops more steeply than the designed bed slope of the canal, a 'fall' or 'drop' structure is built to lower the water level safely without causing erosion.

q: 5. A type II siphon aqueduct is also called .............
explain: In some technical classifications, a Type II siphon aqueduct (where the canal is flumed but the banks are not) is referred to as an under tunnel, as the drain water is passed under the canal.

q: 6. Canal siphon is selected as the suitable cross drainage work when the full supply level in the canal is .............
options: below the bed level of the drain
above the bed level of the drain but below the high flood level
explain: In a canal siphon, the canal water itself is depressed under the drain because the canal's Full Supply Level (FSL) is higher than the bed level of the drain.

q: 7. In the type III aqueduct, the splay of the upstream transition canal is generally taken as .............
explain: When fluming a canal, the transition from the normal width to the flumed width at the entry (upstream) is usually designed with a splay of 2:1.

q: 8. For a given depth of flow in a canal the velocity which keeps the canal free from silting and scouring is called .............
explain: Critical velocity (Vo) is the mean velocity in a channel which will just keep the channel free from both silting and scouring.

q: 9. Borrow pits should preferably be taken from the .............
options: field on the left side of the canal
field on the right side of the canal
field on the left as well as right of the canal
central half width of the section of the canal
explain: To minimize land acquisition costs and simplify logistics, soil for canal banks is ideally borrowed from the center of the canal bed itself where it will eventually be underwater.

q: 10. Bed bars are provided in a canal .............
options: to watch the general behaviour of the canal
explain: Bed bars are masonry or concrete blocks built flush with the design bed level. they serve as permanent reference points to monitor whether the canal is silting or scouring over time.

q: 11. The flow in a canal siphon is .............
explain: In a canal siphon, the canal is taken under a drain. Since the water travels through a barrel below its normal hydraulic gradient, it flows under pipe pressure rather than as an open channel.

q: 12. A canal aligned approximately parallel to the natural drainage of a country is a called
explain: Side slope canals are aligned perpendicular to contours (parallel to drainage lines) to avoid crossing natural drains.

q: 13. The water shed canal is also called
explain: A ridge canal (watershed canal) is aligned along the highest ridge line, allowing gravity irrigation on both sides.

q: 14. The alignment of a canal
options: should ensure minimum cross drainage works
on a water shed is the most economical
explain: Canal alignment is a multi-objective process balancing cost, drainage crossings, and social/environmental impact.

q: 15. Kennedy gave a relation between
options: critical velocity and the depth of flowing water
explain: Kennedy's fundamental equation ($V_0 = 0.55D^{0.64}$) relates the critical velocity (no silting, no scouring) to the depth of water ($D$).

q: 16. The relation given by Kennedy for critical velocity in m/s is
explain: This is the standard formula where 'm' is the critical velocity ratio and 'D' is the depth.

q: 17. Escapes are also known as ............. for the canals.
explain: They protect the canal banks from overtopping and breaching during emergency conditions.

q: 18. In a Sarda type fall, the width of the trapezoidal crest (B) is given by
explain: This empirical formula is used to calculate the stable top width of the crest for a trapezoidal Sarda fall.

q: 19. The Ingles type fall makes use of ............. impact for energy dissipation.
explain: The Ingles (or baffle) fall uses a vertical impact of the water jet against a baffle wall to dissipate kinetic energy.

q: 20. A canal outlet should
options: be so designed that the farmer cannot temper with its functioning
be simple so that it can be constructed or fabricated by local masons
draw its fair share of silt carried by the distributing channel
explain: A good outlet (module) must be tamper-proof, simple, and proportional in silt and water distribution.

q: 21. The ratio between the depths of water levels over crest on the downstream and upstream of the module, is known as .............
explain: The drowning ratio refers to the ratio of the depth of water on the downstream side of the crest to the depth on the upstream side.

q: 22. A weir fails due to .............
options: rupture of floor due to uplift
rupture of floor due to suction caused by standing wave
scour on the upstream and downstream of the weir
explain: Weirs can fail through subsurface causes (uplift/piping) or surface causes (scouring and impact from hydraulic jumps/standing waves).

q: 23. Canals taken off from ice-fed perennial rivers, are known .............
explain: Perennial canals receive a constant supply of water year-round because their source rivers are fed by melting glaciers/snow.

q: 24. If V0 is the critical velocity of a channel, its silt transporting power, according to Kennedy, is proportional to .............
explain: Kennedy's theory suggests that the silt-carrying capacity (silt load) of a channel is proportional to $V_0^{2.5}$ or $V_0^{5/2}$.

q: 25. Regime conditions in a channel may occur if .............
options: channel flows uniformly in incoherent alluvium as that transported in suspension
silt grade and silt charge are constant
explain: A 'true regime' channel requires stability in discharge, sediment type, and sediment volume to prevent silting or scouring.

q: 26. If average particle size of the silt in millimeters is m, the Lacey's silt factor f is proportional to .............
explain: Lacey's silt factor formula is $f = 1.76 \sqrt{m}$, meaning it is proportional to the square root of the mean particle size.

q: 27. Side slope generally kept for canals in loam soil are .............
explain: Slopes in cutting can be steeper (1:1) because the natural soil is compact, whereas filling requires flatter slopes (1.5:1) for stability.

q: 28. The width of a dowla is generally kept between 30 to 60 cm and its height above the road level should invariably be more than .............
explain: A dowla is a small protective ridge on the edge of the service road. A height of 30 cm is required for safety and to prevent runoff into the canal.

q: 29. A fall in a canal bed is generally provided, if .............
options: ground slope exceeds the designed bed slope
designed bed slope exceeds the ground slope
ground slope is practically the same as the designed bed slope
explain: When the natural ground falls more steeply than the required canal bed slope, a 'fall' or 'drop' structure is built to step the water down safely.

q: 30. A current meter measures the velocity of flow, if it is held .............
options: at any point within the cross-section
explain: Current meters are versatile instruments designed to measure local flow velocity at any specific depth or horizontal position in a channel.

q: 31. If the height of the hydraulic gradient line above the floor of thickness l is h and the specific gravity of the material of the floor is G, the minimum thickness t of the floor downstream of the crest is given by the equation .............
explain: The floor thickness must counter the uplift pressure. The formula $t = (h-1)/(G-1)$ ensures the weight of the concrete balances the net upward force.

q: 32. In a Sarda type fall, the rectangular crest, may be used for discharge upto .............
explain: Rectangular crests are efficient for lower discharges; once the discharge exceeds 14 cumecs, a trapezoidal crest is usually preferred.

q: 33. In Montague type fall .............
explain: Montague falls use a parabolic glacis to ensure the water profile follows the structure closely, increasing energy dissipation efficiency.

q: 34. In a canal siphon, the flow is .............
explain: In a siphon, the canal is enclosed in a barrel and flows full under pressure, similar to flow in a pipe.

q: 35. Retrogression of the bed level of a river downstream a weir, occurs due to .............
explain: When clear water (silt-free) is discharged over a weir, it has high capacity to pick up sediment, causing the downstream bed to scour or retrogress.

q: 36. According to Lacey, depth of scour in a river depends upon the straightness of the reach. If D is the depth of scour in regime flow in a right angled bend, it is .............
explain: Lacey suggested multipliers for scour depth based on river curvature; for sharp right-angled bends, the scour depth is taken as 2.0 times the normal regime depth.
